title: Degeneracy of continuum-polymer cutoff partition functions when the dimension-dependent critical small-jump condition fails
difficulty_reason: H2: positive-martingale convergence does not itself show the limit vanishes. The author changes to the size-biased environment, represents it by an independent Poisson process planted along a Brownian path, and reduces degeneration to total-variation separation from the original environment. The independent core constructs dimension-specific separating statistics and tunes a slowly diverging spatial window so the squared mean shift dominates both variances: cone point counts ford>=3, weighted small jumps ford1, and a time-jump weighted statistic exposing the critical logarithmic factor ford2. The full proof treats the initially finite large-jump first moment case and then removes that intermediate assumption by double truncation/Doob tail control. This statistic/spine separation is an independent nonroutineH2 mechanism; it does not inherit old2090H3 good-trajectory/replica multibody UI difficulty, and the elementary Mecke moment computation is supporting material, not another item.
